title: 60% or 50%: who ends with the money?
hook: Two bettors, nearly the same belief, the same money. Bet against each other for 500 races.

knows: betting odds are the wealth-weighted average belief (odds-average-the-bettors)
repeated bets multiply your money rather than add to it
doesNotKnow: that repeated betting shifts wealth toward the more accurate bettor, so prices drift toward the truth, though luck can lead for a long time

misconception: Two bettors with similar beliefs will keep similar wealth.
objective: The learner can explain that each race multiplies the ratio of two bettors' money by how well each belief fit the result, so a small edge in accuracy compounds until the accurate bettor holds nearly all the money and the odds approach the truth, even though luck can favour the other bettor for hundreds of races.

claims.text: In all five seeded runs of 500 races, the 60% bettor ended with at least 98.8% of the money (98.8% to over 99.9%).
claims.source: Demo.tsx run(): mulberry32 seeds 2211 to 2215 (consecutive seeds fixed by the brief, not picked by the builder), one rng() per race, win if < 0.6. Share at race 500: 0.999905, 0.987766, 0.999678, 1.000000 (rounded), 0.991811. Matches the brief's check in company/domains/briefs/economics.markets.md #21. · Fact-check pass 23 2026-10-14: Own mulberry32 copy of run(): race-500 shares 0.999905, 0.987766, 0.999678, 1.000000, 0.991811; pct() gives 98.8% low, 'over 99.9%' high.

claims.text: Luck can lead for a long time: after race 50, the 50% bettor's best moment was 91.0% of the money at race 203 in run 2 (seed 2212) and 94.2% at race 176 in run 5 (seed 2215); runs 1, 3 and 4 never put the 50% bettor above half after race 50.
claims.source: Demo.tsx RUNS[1][200] = 0.113561, so the 50% bettor holds 0.886. Seed 2212 is quoted because it shows a long lucky lead (disclose-chosen-seeds); in run 5 (seed 2215) the 50% bettor also led after race 50 (69.8% at race 200). · Fact-check pass 23 2026-10-14: Own run: seed 2212, race 200, 50% bettor holds 0.8864 (88.6%); seed 2215 0.6981; only runs 2 and 5 dip below half after race 50, so the luck-run milestone is reachable. | REWORDED v2 (demo-builder, 2026-10-14): v2 quotes the circled low point of the run the learner is looking at (lowPoint() over races 51..t, computed from state), not race 200. Builder's node replay of run(): run 2 min share 0.090 at race 203 (50% bettor 91.0%), run 5 min 0.058 at race 176 (94.2%); other runs' minima after race 50 are 0.716, 0.655, 0.553 (above half). Seeds 2211-2215 fixed by the brief. Unverified.

claims.text: In this model each race multiplies the ratio of the 60% bettor's money to the 50% bettor's by 1.2 on a win and 0.8 on a loss; three wins and two losses multiply it by 1.11. In run 1 (seed 2211) race 1 is a loss, so the single-race step shows ×0.8.
claims.source: Winners split the pool by stake, so the ratio changes by 0.6/0.5 = 1.2 on a win and 0.4/0.5 = 0.8 on a loss, whatever the shares. 1.2^3 × 0.8^2 = 1.1059. Demo.tsx WIN_X, LOSS_X. · Fact-check pass 23 2026-10-14: Re-derived: winners split the pool by stake, so the money ratio changes by 0.6/0.5 = 1.2 on a win and 0.4/0.5 = 0.8 on a loss at any share (node check at a = 0.3 gives 1.2); 1.2^3 x 0.8^2 = 1.10592, shown as 1.11. | REWORDED v2 (demo-builder, 2026-10-14): v2 adds the single-race step and its caption/readout. Builder's node replay: seed 2211's first rng() is not under 0.6, so race 1 is a loss; ratio a/(1-a) goes 1.00 -> 0.80. The reveal quotes the recorded first single race. Unverified.

claims.text: The pool's win odds are the money-weighted average belief, so as money moves to the 60% bettor the odds move toward the true 60%.
claims.source: With everyone betting all their money, the share of the pool on 'win' is 0.6·a + 0.5·(1 − a), where a is the 60% bettor's share (Demo.tsx readout). As a → 1 this → 0.6. · Fact-check pass 23 2026-10-14: Re-derived: everyone bets everything, so the share of the pool on 'win' is 0.6a + 0.5(1 - a), the readout's formula; it tends to 0.6 as a tends to 1.

claims.text: The market is a simplified model: two bettors, no fees, each bets all their money every race, split by belief.
claims.source: Stage chip and reveal footnote; Demo.tsx run(). · Fact-check pass 23 2026-10-14: Stage chip 'Model: each bets everything, split by belief' and reveal footnote 'two bettors, no fees, everyone bets everything each race' match run().

claims.text: Stage captions: a single race reads 'Race t: win/loss, money ratio ×1.2/×0.8'; a jump reads 'Races a–b: w wins ×1.2, l losses ×0.8: ratio ×(1.2^w × 0.8^l)'. The money ratio readout is the 60% bettor's money divided by the 50% bettor's.
claims.source: Demo.tsx v2 msg and Readout 'Money ratio, 60% : 50%' = share/(1-share). Product follows from c3 (each race multiplies the ratio by 1.2 or 0.8 whatever the shares). Values of 1,000 or more print as '1,000+'. Builder, 2026-10-14.

recall.question: Two bettors keep betting all their money against each other on the same event. One's belief is slightly closer to the true chance. After a very long time, what is most likely?
options: They stay roughly even, since their beliefs are close
The closer one holds nearly all the money
Whoever is ahead after the first 100 bets stays ahead
recall.why: Each bet multiplies the ratio of their money by how well each belief fit the result. A small edge compounds; luck can lead for a while but not forever.
